2610.04292.title: LMBuild: Evaluating LLM Agents for Generating Buildable and Functional Structures
2610.04292.paper_summary: LLM-based agents are increasingly capable of generating complex 3D structures, with the potential to reshape how objects are designed and realized in the physical world. Yet, producing elegant geometry is fundamentally different from producing objects that can be built and perform their intended functions. Existing evaluations largely focus on geometric quality while overlooking physical realizability. We introduce LMBuild, a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on generating buildable and functional structures. LMBuild represents generated objects as assembled structures comprising part decompositions, joints, materials, and sequences. To support reproducible evaluation, we provide a unified framework consisting of: (1) an interactive environment in which agents can use tools to retrieve, create, and place components to construct objects; (2) a curated benchmark that repurposes established CAD datasets and augments them with knowledge from Wikipedia; and (3) a evaluation framework covering structural soundness, functional affordance, design quality, and physical realization. Evaluations across 30 systems reveal several intriguing findings: (a) Soundness and alignment are no longer the primary bottlenecks for frontier closed-source models, while functional affordance and physical operability remain substantially more challenging; (b) stronger models more effectively create new components, whereas weaker models tend to rely on retrieval; and (c) providing functional specifications substantially improves part completeness, kinematics, and physical operability. These results show that generating real-world structures requires deeper reasoning about functional affordances, mechanics, and designing and creating novel components. We expect LMBuild to provide a foundation for measuring progress and incentivizing research toward agents that generate buildable and functional structures.
2610.04292.paper_summary_zh: LLM 基礎的代理人越來越能夠生成複雜的 3D 結構，具有重新塑造物體在物理世界中設計和實現方式的潛力。<lb/>然而，生成優雅的幾何形狀與生成可以建造並執行其預期功能的物體在根本上是不同的。<lb/>現有的評估主要集中在幾何質量上，而忽略了物理可實現性。<lb/>我們介紹了 LMBuild，這是一個用於評估 LLM 代理人生成可建造和功能性結構的基準。<lb/>LMBuild 將生成的物體表示為由部件分解、接頭、材料和序列組成的組裝結構。<lb/>為了支持可重複的評估，我們提供了一個統一的框架，包括：<lb/>(1) 一個互動環境，代理人可以使用工具來檢索、創建和放置組件以構建物體；<lb/>(2) 一個策劃的基準，重新利用已建立的 CAD 數據集並用來自維基百科的知識進行增強；<lb/>(3) 一個評估框架，涵蓋結構健全性、功能可用性、設計質量和物理實現。<lb/>對 30 個系統的評估揭示了幾個有趣的發現：<lb/>(a) 健全性和對齊不再是前沿封閉源模型的主要瓶頸，而功能可用性和物理操作性仍然相對更具挑戰性；<lb/>(b) 更強的模型更有效地創建新組件，而較弱的模型則傾向於依賴檢索；<lb/>(c) 提供功能規範顯著提高了部件的完整性、運動學和物理操作性。<lb/>這些結果表明，生成現實世界的結構需要對功能可用性、機械學以及設計和創建新組件進行更深入的推理。<lb/>我們期望 LMBuild 能夠為衡量進展和激勵研究提供基礎，以促進生成可建造和功能性結構的代理人。
